newsitem.title: UK: Brent paper spreads firmer, Dated holds steady.
newsitem.headline: Brent paper spreads firmer, Dated holds steady.

text.p: Brent paper spreads were firmer on Wednesday despite a persistent overhang of September Brent cargoes, though traders saw Dated Brent holding steady with refinery distillate stocks low and crude supplies tight.
Oct/Nov traded at +52 cents early in the day then at +55. CFDs also improved with two deals for Sept 23-27 dates done at Nov +20 and Nov +23 cents.

"I still think middle distillate fundamentals look very good with the onset of autumn and winter...but the market has lost the political froth so it's difficult to judge what it will do next," a wet trader said.

One million barrels of Sept 28-30 Brent was sold late on Tuesday for about Nov Brent +15 cents, equivalent to Oct -35/40 cents. A major was offering Brent at the equivalent of Nov Brent +26 cents on Wednesday, traders said.
The seller, a Wall Street refiner, kept the sole Brent cargo which turned wet on Wednesday taking the trader's total tally to four Brent cargoes.

"It did look sloppy on the Brent if we hit paper -45 cents but at that level you would expect to see a floor. I think you could only go below that if the market was full of oil and storage tanks were full," a trader for a European company said.

Nov Brent was talked around $22.25/30 a barrel late in the afternoon after IPE futures opened higher on the back of U.S. weekly stocks data showing a lower than expected build in distillates for this time of year.
Sweet grades were also in favour in the Med, where traders cited the imminent switch in Europe to 0.05 percent sulphur content as the main reason.
"A lot of people are talking about the switch in sulphur specs and this is the principle swing to the sweet crude interest," a trader said.
